0.content:
Khaenri'ah (also: Khaenriah, Kingdom of Khaenri'ah, Dahri): Khaenri'ah was a kingdom of humans deep underground beneath the Sumeru desert. It was the one nation in Teyvat that never had a god. Its people built machines, worked alchemy that could create life, and dreamed of standing above the gods' order; Dainsleif calls it "the pride of humankind." Five hundred years ago its rulers' use of Abyssal power set off the cataclysm, and the Heavenly Principles and the gods destroyed it. Its survivors were cursed: pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns cannot die, and those of mixed blood became monsters. In Sumeru it is also called Dahri.

Two royal lines ruled it: first the Crimson Moon Dynasty, then the Eclipse Dynasty, whose last Vinster King was Irmin. Pure-blooded Khaenri'ahns are marked by four-pointed star pupils. Ruin Machines, the Abyss Order and the hilichurls all come from Khaenri'ah, and so do Dainsleif, Kaeya's family and the Fatui Director Pierro. In 7.1 it was revealed that all Khaenri'ahns descend from the Tsaritsa Anastasya and the Third Descender Saarelainen, which is why they honour her as the "Mother of Khaenri'ah".

Geography: A subterranean realm beneath the Sumeru desert, dark and almost barren of natural life. Kaeya says only that it was "deep underground somewhere near Sumeru". A great sealed gate in Gavireh Lajavard, in the Girdle of the Sands, is said to lead down to the ruined kingdom.

People: Khaenri'ahns descend from Anastasya and Saarelainen. Pure-bloods count as a people distinct from the surface nations: their pupils are four-pointed stars, while descendants of the Crimson Moon Dynasty have red X-shaped pupils. A heavily diluted bloodline may show no mark at all. Outsiders from the surface also came to live in Khaenri'ah; in the legend Perinheri, a princess who would not submit to Morax drifts in through its gates. Khaenri'ahns whose ancestry lay in the gods' lands were later cursed differently from pure-bloods.

Government: Khaenri'ah was a hereditary monarchy. In the Eclipse era the "Vinster King" ruled with the Court of Khaenri'ah. Under him were royal mages (Hroptatyr was Chief Royal Mage), the Universitas Magistrorum, several knightly orders, and an intelligence service. Irmin was the last king, and his closest advisers were Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir.

Religion: No god ever ruled Khaenri'ah. It was not abandoned by one; it never had one. Its people suspected that the Heavenly Principles were outsiders who had usurped the world, knew the rumour that Teyvat's sky is false, and planned to rise above "the fundamental principles" of the world. The motto behind the war machines was that land is not tilled with farm tools but won "with steel and blood."

Technology: Khaenri'ah built the war automatons now called Ruin Machines. The Ruin Guard's original name was "Field Tiller". The machines can repair themselves and keep working for centuries. After the fall they wandered Teyvat without a purpose and gathered at ruins. Its alchemy, the Art of Khemia, could create life, which mattered in a land with little natural life.

History: Khaenri'ah was founded as a godless nation around the time Sal Vindagnyr fell, thousands of years ago. The Crimson Moon Dynasty ruled first and was overthrown by the Eclipse Dynasty. Five hundred years ago King Irmin named the newly arrived Traveler's sibling his heir and "Savior", then used them as a vessel to absorb unlimited Abyssal power. When he blinded Vedrfolnir for warning him, Dainsleif and four others stormed the palace. All five turned on Dainsleif and took the Abyssal power, becoming the Five Sinners. Abyssal monsters poured across Teyvat, Celestia and the gods destroyed the kingdom, and Ronova cursed its people.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 Khaenri'ah lies in ruins and its gate is sealed. It has not been visited in the main story. Its survivors are scattered and cursed, the Abyss Order fights to revive it, and its final Archon Quest chapter is announced but not released.

The Heavenly Principles have been asleep since the cataclysm. In 7.1 Anastasya concluded that destroying Khaenri'ah triggered the Third Descender's curse, which had been meant to protect his descendants. The Abyss Order, led by the Traveler's sibling, holds the woven ley lines of a "New Khaenri'ah" and is looking for somewhere to lay them down.

1.content: The Crimson Moon Dynasty was Khaenri'ah's first known royal line. It ruled when "a crimson moon shone" over the underground realm. Its priests had the people worship the Crimson Moon, the Abyss-fused remains of the Iridescent Moon, and its royal blood carries the Abyssal "Balemoon Bloodfire". The dynasty sealed the Crimson Moon and its corrupted Moon Marrow inside a domain that only the Bloodfire can open. Alchemy and the warbeasts of the Beastmaster Knights flourished. A coup put the Eclipse Dynasty on the throne. Arlecchino suggests the usurpers opposed a direct link to the Abyss, or that an ideological split drove them. Irmin later ordered its descendants exterminated, yet the line survives in Arlecchino.

2.comment: Khaenri'ah: Eclipse Dynasty and King Irmin
2.content: The Eclipse Dynasty (literally "Black Sun") replaced the Crimson Moon Dynasty and ruled until the cataclysm. It favoured mechanical engineering and, at the end, "secrets from beyond the skies." Its last Vinster King, the one-eyed Irmin, trusted Hroptatyr and Vedrfolnir above all. He made the Traveler's sibling his heir, used them to absorb Abyssal power, turned the Universitas over to Abyssal research, and blinded Vedrfolnir for prophesying ruin. His fate after the palace coup is unclear.

3.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah
3.content: The Five Sinners were among Khaenri'ah's most esteemed people: Rhinedottir "Gold" (Life), Vedrfolnir "The Visionary" (Time), Surtalogi "The Foul" (Void), Hroptatyr "The Wise" (Reason) and Rerir "Rächer of Solnari" (Death). Dainsleif gathered them to rescue his brother. Instead, each took one sixth of the world-shattering Abyssal power Irmin had poured into the Traveler's sibling. None defended Khaenri'ah as it fell. Hroptatyr was one of the "four pillars" of the kingdom.

4.content: The Universitas Magistrorum was the kingdom's royal academy, directly under the king. It worked in astrology, alchemy and other arts, and also trained fighters. In the last years Hroptatyr was its president and Eftirvit (Pierro) its vice-president. Both had studied under Professor Mimameith, who fell fatally ill after working on the king's Abyssal research. When Irmin became obsessed with the Abyss, all staff were moved to Abyssal research except the Moon Marrow researcher Tholindis.

5.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Schwanenritter and the Exodus to Sumeru
5.content: As dark beasts overran the kingdom, Knight Marshal Anfortas declared himself Regent. His Schwanenritter ("Swan Knights") led able-bodied survivors to the surface through the Girdle of the Sands into Sumeru, fighting with Ruin Golems they called "Mechanical Wardens". On the surface many refugees fell ill and turned into monsters. The knights fought on in Dharma Forest beside the sage Nagarjuna, who named them "heroes of Dahri". Ynghildr vanished in battle and Hildric died of illness. Anfortas killed the traitor Hadura, losing his left eye, gave him a knight's funeral anyway, and fought alone until his presumed death.

6.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Royal Guard and the Black Serpents
6.content: The Black Serpent Knights were the royal guard, with Dainsleif, the "Twilight Sword", as captain. During the cataclysm Dainsleif ordered his knight Halfdan to protect the people at all costs. The curse turned the guard into Shadowy Husks and eroded knights who have lost most of their memories. In the Chasm, Halfdan's band still guarded hilichurls as Khaenri'ahn citizens, until Dainsleif released him. Dainsleif could make out only one word of their speech in the old tongue: "run".

7.content: After the Traveler's sibling arrived, Irmin and the court proclaimed them heir to the throne and a prophesied "Savior" who would bring the kingdom a bright future. A young Dainsleif attended the ceremony. Ordinary people hoped too: Direidyth's grandmother told her stories of a Savior who would rescue Khaenri'ahns at doomsday. Through a time overlap Istaroth arranged in present-day Natlan, Direidyth met the Traveler. When she later told the sibling about it, the sibling left Khaenri'ah to find their twin.

8.content: In 7.1 Rhinedottir told the Tsaritsa that every Khaenri'ahn descends from her and the Third Descender, Saarelainen. (The trailer "Sudden Snow" shows that their son had four-pointed star pupils.) To restore Anastasya after the Heavenly Principles erased her, Saarelainen gave his body to become the seven Gnoses. In return he secured a promise that his descendants would never be harmed, backed by a curse that would strike if the promise broke. Anastasya concluded that the cataclysm triggered it, putting the Heavenly Principles to sleep. She knew of the bloodline but had no memory of it. Khaenri'ahns honour her as "Mother of Khaenri'ah", and Dainsleif came to an audience with her for that reason.

9.comment: Khaenri'ah: The Curses on the Khaenri'ahns
9.content: After the cataclysm Ronova, the Shade of Death, cursed every Khaenri'ahn. Pure-bloods were judged "the greater sinners" and given immortality: they cannot die or age, but they still suffer erosion, which wears down body and mind. Most became Abyss Mages, Heralds and Lectors. Those descended from people of the gods' lands received the "curse of the wilderness" and turned into hilichurls.

10.content: The Abyss Order wants to revive Khaenri'ah and take revenge on The Seven and Celestia. With the Loom of Fate, the Traveler's sibling wove ley lines for a new Khaenri'ah inside Natlan's Night Kingdom, building on an Inteyvat flower and on memories of the kingdom from Order members and Dainsleif. The result, the Atlas of the New World, holds those ley lines and still needs a place to be laid down. The sibling means to face the Heavenly Principles "as equals" with a whole world behind them.

11.content: The Inteyvat is Khaenri'ah's national flower, five petals in white and pale blue, and it once bloomed all over the kingdom. Dainsleif says it wilts after two weeks. Plucked and carried out of Khaenri'ah, its petals turn hard, and they only soften and crumble to dust once returned home, so it stands for a wanderer far from home. Lumine wears one in her hair.
